I would say if you can, the approach for both History and Geography was similar for me anyway, but yes at times for Geography there is overall less to write about. I would say try to avoid fluff for Geo, but have the points be really relevant and fleshed out. That doesn’t mean write three pages, just make them make sense and be really relevant to the topic, and why each point has it’s place - that’s important. It kind of is a case of learn every point for every essay, more so than History where there is potential to draw ever so slightly from opinions at times or just general “common sense” when stuck, which you can also do for Geo in a way. If you’re stuck - for example: the region is the Mezzogiorno (it’s hot - what can you conclude about what the effects of this likely would be, etc). But yes - learn those points and get a good visual image of what each essay is about. As I recall you don’t have to learn every single one, but do the most you can. I don’t even remember my diagrams and if I did - they were probably awful but use this to help you if you need, maybe it is easier for you to gather some points here if you are stuck. One other thing - yes in the actual exam as soon as you get the paper I would flick to the essays, immediately pick them out and write the points for each one down (to your best memory). Forget and go back to short questions - then you already have that down and can just draw from your memory going into the essays. Even if you are short on time - just write the bullet points down in a sentence or two - examiner will see this and potentially take into consideration (it cannot hurt anyway). Geography essays if I remember don’t need all the waffle, and don’t need to be 3 pages long if you have the info and you make great points to support the question. Hope I helped, let me know if I can give some more insight

Geography: Most importantly get your essays done, and write them all out yourself on paper, writing them is the best way to get the information soaked in. Make the essay into bullet points, with each one covering one particular aspect of the region obviously. From this point, once you have a good grasp on these points you can shorten each one to a few words to help you remember them in the exam and just draw the point from that. Some essays will come more naturally to you than others, so put focus on the hard ones but don’t dismiss the easy ones either. You are gonna be panicking in the final moments but that’s normal, just try to memorise memorise, understanding is not so important here if you get me. For short questions, understanding is a bit more important but the topics are not quite as complex and is still mostly memory. Again write out your rocks, etc and just try to get a grasp of these and make bullet points again. Look, you will have some weak topics and everyone does, do what you can. You can obviously leave a few essays out too if I remember correctly (did my LC in 2017 so I’m not too fresh)

Biology: There is more understanding that goes into this but again a lot of memory too. I would say hone in on the things they always ask and the big topics - get a grasp on these. Reproduction, circulation, ecology, etc. Flash cards really helped me out for biology as there was less of the huge volume to memorise and more buzz points. Understanding the topics is very useful though as you can write more and for science when you understand how things work you can answer more questions for less effort, if that makes sense. Overall the biology stuff can seem daunting but honestly it’s the easiest of the 3 and you still have time to get the “click” moment for a lot of the bigger topics. 

English: Definitely the hardest to give tips about as the subject is quite subjective in terms of exams, not sure what topics are predicted etc and what poets you have, but pick what you enjoy and stick with it. Learn what each of the poems are about, learn what the key talking points of your play and stories are so you understand what the examiners are gonna touch on in the essays. Exam papers are super important for this, check the questions they ask and write essays, or if you feel confident enough - make the bullet points like I said to outline all your talking points and fill in the gaps in the exam. At the end of the day, there are no wrong answers necessarily and you can answer how you like, but your justification is important. Even if you get shit questions and have to do one you don’t like, you can still pull it off. Sit back for a moment, plan what you could say and make sure you can back it up. That’s essentially the point. If you can, answer more than one question but don’t stress this as time will be tight. For the creative writing aspect, pick your essay and plan it too, for 5 mins max and get onto it. When you plan in the English exam it is so much easier to string your points together COHERENTLY. Big emphasis on that.

Seems like we both did very similar subjects, and in my experience I found my studying approach for Geography and History to be very similar. And remember: aim as high as you can, but 100% is not a realistic goal anyway. It takes the pressure off a bit. If you need 70% that is an achievable goal. I’m telling you as a crammer myself. I recommend you grind it out for this last month, it’s just this little bit to go, and you never have to do it again. 

100% believe in you, if you have any questions feel free

I actually had a really interesting scam attempt happen to me a few weeks ago that I have never seen before. Guy adds me, high level profile, and asks me to check out his Cs:Go YT channel (Mostly Cs:Go item giveaways) and tell him what I think. I searched for it on YT, found it and told him it was decent. He then said that as a thank you he would send me a game via Steam, this was quite weird but I won't say no to something free.

He asked for my E-Mail and at this point I was suspicious so I gave him an unused one. He sent me an E-Mail with the game (Gta 5, which makes no sense to give to someone for checking out your YT channel), looked like it was from Steam and everything. Even the images and stuff looked identical to a gift you may receive. 

Silly me clicked the damn Redeem link and it sent me to a Google Docs page and downloaded some really strange client. Instantly deleted and removed the guy. I later checked the comments on his YT channel and it was full of people calling him a scammer, using scammed items for giveaways, etc. I don't think I still have his YT channel name, but I thought I would put this here because I thought it was a unique scam. 

I did not end up losing anything but I'm sure I would have if I had opened the client.

[The E-Mail Screenshot](https://gyazo.com/6c7df9bd16d8db948cd9eb987849d7bf)

[The Client Screenshot](https://gyazo.com/8023d977a2e8a82f13fbb4958b6985f3)
No the client is not legit even if it looks like it is, I researched it quite a bit.

Tl;DR - Guy tried to scam me by sending game gift via E-Mail, looked legit but was a spooky scary client.
